samples.summary: Compatibility asymmetry: the backend deliberately keeps serving nonce-less CLI logins so published CLIs do not break, but the new CLI hard-fails against any server that does not yet echo the nonce — it 403s the callback, never settles, and only reports after the 30s timeout. Users on a self-hosted or not-yet-deployed backend cannot log in at all with a freshly installed CLI. The design doc records this as intentional ("Upgrade the server"), but it is the mirror image of the compatibility argument used to justify the server-side leniency, and no version-negotiation or grace path is offered.
samples.evidence: login.ts nonce check `if (!nonce || !nonceMatches(...)) { 403; return; }` plus the timeout branch; docs/design/cli.md:900-906.

samples.summary: Scope: the change bundles four largely independent concerns — the exit-code contract (the originating issue), an SSRF gate on export image URLs, nonce-bound OAuth login (CLI + backend + store + guard), and an `HttpClient` refactor routing API-key endpoints through `send()`. The task lessons doc justifies the two security controls, but the combination makes the diff hard to review as one unit and pulls backend auth changes into a CLI exit-code issue.
samples.evidence: errors.ts + image-fetcher.ts SSRF gate + backend auth nonce + http-client sendJson refactor in one change.

samples.summary: Reuse: internal/private-address gating for attacker-influenced image URLs now exists twice in the repo with two different designs — the backend's `miro.service.ts` host allowlist (guarding the same class of SSRF for board image URLs) and this new denylist/DNS-resolution gate in the CLI. Neither lives in `@wafflebase/core`, so the rules will drift. A shared helper (or at least a cross-reference between the two designs) would fit the repo's stated reuse expectation.

Behavior change beyond the stated intent: `mode=cli` with a missing/invalid port previously fell through silently to the ordinary web OAuth flow; it now throws a 400. That is consistent with rest-api.md's port range statement, but it is a compatibility-affecting change made in the same breath as an argument that published CLIs must not be 400'd, and neither design doc calls out the new hard failure for a nonce-less/portless `mode=cli` request.
samples.evidence: guard: `if (!Number.isInteger(portNum) || portNum < 1024 || portNum > 65535) throw new BadRequestException('Invalid CLI port')` replacing the previous conditional injection.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. docs/design/cli.md:1182 contains the row "Fontkit font load failure | 2 | FONT_LOAD_ERROR | (after fallback exhausted)" inside the canonical "### 10. Error Matrix" (cli.md:1161). A repo-wide grep for FONT_LOAD_ERROR returns that doc line only — nothing in packages/cli emits it, while every neighbouring row's code is grounded in code (INVALID_DOCX docx-import.ts:85, IMAGE_URL_BLOCKED image-fetcher.ts:62, CONFIRMATION_REQ import.ts:131), so the row is an outlier rather than a doc-wide aspirational convention. Behavior contradicts it: classifiedFontFetch (pdf-export.ts:27-46) yields SystemError NETWORK_ERROR/SERVER_ERROR via fetchOrThrow (errors.ts:165) and httpError (errors.ts:75-84), and httpError returns a plain Error for 4xx → exit 1 via exitCodeFor (errors.ts:180-188); the non-HTTP font-load path throws a plain Error at fontkit-measurer.ts:68, which is exactly the documented case, also exit 1 with no code. The originating task (20260803-cli-system-exit-code-todo.md:1-16,42-43,61) exists to close documented-contract-without-implementation gaps in this very doc and marks "design doc updated" done, so leaving this row unreconciled is a spec-conformance / design-doc-discipline miss in this lens, major by kind. No guard, no alternate emitter, not absent, not unreachable — nothing supports a refutation.

Users on a self-hosted or not-yet-deployed backend cannot log in at all with a freshly installed CLI. The design doc records this as intentional ("Upgrade the server"), but it is the mirror image of the compatibility argument used to justify the server-side leniency, and no version-negotiation or grace path is offered.
finding.evidence: login.ts nonce check `if (!nonce || !nonceMatches(...)) { 403; return; }` plus the timeout branch; docs/design/cli.md:900-906.

verdict.reason: The code exists exactly as quoted (login.ts:306-315 403s a nonce-less callback without settling; :362-381 reports it only at the 30s timeout), so the behavior is real. But it is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. (a) The originating issue (docs/tasks/active/20260803-cli-system-exit-code-todo.md:1-51) is the 0/1/2 exit-code contract; it states no compatibility acceptance criterion, and its checklist line 64 explicitly sanctions the nonce-bound callback, so no acceptance criterion is unmet. (b) Design-doc discipline is satisfied: the canonical subsystem doc docs/design/cli.md:890-919 (no parallel doc) records the CLI-side enforcement AND the server-side leniency together with the reasoning that server-side rejection "buys nothing it costs" since an attacker controlling the loopback port picks their own nonce; the same rationale is in packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:18-31 and the lessons file docs/tasks/active/20260803-cli-system-exit-code-lessons.md:34-46,84-91, where this exact tradeoff was already litigated and settled. (c) No Non-Goal is exceeded (docs/design/cli.md:55-69 says nothing about old-backend compatibility) and nothing is duplicated. The finding is a request to revisit a documented deliberate tradeoff and add an unrequested version-negotiation/grace path — a preference about approach, i.e. minor kind under this rubric, which never blocks. Fail-open-vs-fail-closed merits belong to the security lens.

finding.summary: Backend CLI-auth API contract change (nonce now required; echoed on the loopback redirect) is not reflected in the canonical backend surface doc
finding.evidence: `docs/design/rest-api.md:285-297` is the doc that owns the CLI auth endpoints ("the backend surface is:") and cli.md:190 explicitly defers to it ("CSRF and port-validation details live in rest-api.md 'CLI Auth Endpoints'"). This change makes `GET /auth/github?mode=cli` reject requests without `nonce=[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,128}` with a 400 (github-auth.guard.ts), and makes the callback redirect `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=…&nonce=…` (auth.controller.ts:127-134). rest-api.md still documents `GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>` with no nonce, the redirect without `&nonce=`, and its risk table (line 317-318) still lists only port validation and CSRF. Per CONTRIBUTING/design-doc discipline the change to an API contract should be folded into the canonical doc rather than only into cli.md's new §8 addendum.

verdict.reason: The canonical backend-surface doc already documents the nonce contract. docs/design/rest-api.md:334 documents `GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>&nonce=<nonce>`; lines 337-343 specify that nonce is stored alongside the CSRF token, must match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,128}`, that a malformed/repeated one is a 400 minting no state, and that a missing one is accepted with a warning for older published CLIs (with a pointer to cli.md and the condition for making it a hard 400). Lines 344-349 document the callback redirect as `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=<auth-code>&nonce=<nonce>`, with `&nonce=` omitted when the state carries none. The risk table has a dedicated third row at line 377 covering the loopback-code-injection risk mitigated by the nonce, in addition to the port-validation (375) and CSRF (376) rows. The doc also matches the implementation: packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:52-62 only 400s on a malformed nonce and merely logs a warning when nonce is undefined, so the finding's premise that the endpoint now rejects nonce-less requests with 400 is itself incorrect. The reviewer's cited line numbers (285-297, 317-318) correspond to a stale revision; the current section 7 starts at line 328.

finding.summary: Fail-closed nonce requirement breaks already-installed published CLI versions with no compatibility window; the doc's "upgrade the server first" mitigation does not hold for an npm-published CLI
finding.evidence: `packages/cli/package.json` publishes `@wafflebase/cli` 0.6.2 with a `bin` (not private), so users run whatever version they installed. The guard now throws `BadRequestException('Missing or invalid CLI login nonce. Upgrade the `wafflebase` CLI.')` for any `?mode=cli` without a nonce, so every previously released CLI's `login` breaks the moment the server deploys. docs/design/cli.md's new section asserts "Backend and CLI ship from the same tree; upgrade the server first", which is true for the monorepo but not for installed CLIs — no deprecation/transition path (e.g. accept-but-warn for one release) is designed or documented.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. `GitHubAuthGuard` does NOT fail closed on a missing nonce: at github-auth.guard.ts:52-62 a `?mode=cli` request with `nonce === undefined` only logs a warning and continues with `nonce = undefined`; the only throw is `BadRequestException('Invalid CLI login nonce')` for a *malformed* nonce (line 58-59). The exact message the finding quotes ('Missing or invalid CLI login nonce. Upgrade the `wafflebase` CLI.') does not exist anywhere in the repo (repo-wide grep: no matches). The compatibility window the finding says is missing is explicitly designed, documented and tested: guard comment lines 18-30 state the missing-nonce acceptance is deliberate because @wafflebase/cli is published to npm and a hard 400 would break released CLIs; github-auth.guard.spec.ts:70-85 asserts 'still serves a nonce-less CLI login'; auth.controller.ts:130-134 only appends `&nonce=` when present so nonce-less flows still redirect. The quoted doc assertion is also absent — docs/design/cli.md:907-919 says the opposite ('a deliberate compatibility window, not an oversight ... When published CLIs older than nonce-bound login are out of support, the guard can turn the warning into a 400'), and grep for 'upgrade the server first'/'same tree' finds nothing in cli.md. (The CLI is version 0.6.4 at packages/cli/package.json:3, not 0.6.2 as claimed.)
